transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I can’t stop thinking about how rough and worn my face and hands look. The cracks, spots, the sagging… it feels like people notice it right away, especially bankers or county folks I have to deal with. My wife says I just look like a man who’s worked outdoors, but it doesn’t feel that way to me.

Can you tell me more about how these thoughts affect you? Do you find yourself spending a lot of time thinking about these changes in your appearance, or does it feel like they interfere with your daily life?

Yeah… it does get in the way. More than I like to admit.

I’ve missed calls with bankers, put off decisions on the farm, just because I couldn’t get myself looking… decent enough to sit down with people. And I don’t really agree to photos anymore, even ones that would help with the retreat or craft sales. I just avoid it.
Can you tell me more about how avoiding photos or meetings has affected your work on the farm or your relationships with others?

It’s… made things harder than they need to be.

I’ve missed calls with bankers, and I’ve put off some farm decisions because I couldn’t make myself feel like I looked acceptable enough to sit down with people. And with the retreat and craft sales, I’ve stopped agreeing to photos, even though I know they’d help. I just… avoid it.
Do these concerns about your appearance ever make it hard for you to interact with people, even outside of work—like with friends or family?

Some, yeah. I don’t like admitting that.

It’s mostly when I have to be seen or… represent something, I guess. I’ve missed bankers’ calls and put off farm decisions because I couldn’t get myself looking acceptable enough to sit down with people. And I’ve stopped agreeing to photos for the retreat and craft sales, even though I know they’d help. I just avoid it.
When you look at your face or hands, do you notice flaws or defects that others might not even see, or that seem much more obvious to you than they do to other people?

Yeah… I suppose that’s about right.

I get stuck on how rough my face and hands look. The cracks, the spots, the sagging… it feels like anyone I sit across from, bankers or county folks, they’re seeing all of it right away.

My wife says I just look like a man who’s worked outdoors, but… it doesn’t feel that way to me.

When you feel concerned about how your face or hands look, do you find yourself doing anything to try to fix or check those concerns—like looking in mirrors, covering up, or trying to change your appearance in some way?

Yeah… I do some of that.

Before I leave for a loan meeting or if I’m going to sit at a craft-fair table, I’ll check the truck mirror, then the bathroom mirror. More than I should. I’ll mess with my hat, turn it different ways, trying to make my face look less… noticeable, I guess.

And I catch myself looking at my hands next to the younger workers’ hands. Comparing them. It can eat up time I ought to be using on the farm.
How much distress or upset do these concerns about your face and hands cause you when you think about them?

It upsets me more than I like to say.

It’s… kind of what brought me in, really. I can’t seem to get past how worn my face and hands look. The cracks and spots, the sagging. I’ll think some banker or county person is just staring right at it, even though my wife says I just look like somebody who’s worked outdoors.

Still feels pretty bad when I’m in it.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest or pleasure in most activities, even things you used to enjoy?

I don’t know… not in a big way, I guess.

I still get things done. I wouldn’t say I’m hopeless. Some days I’m quieter than others, but… I haven’t really thought of it like that.
When you look at your face or hands, do you feel like they look abnormal, unattractive, or somehow broken in a way that makes you feel like people will judge you negatively because of it?

Yeah… I guess I do.

It’s mostly that my face and hands look so rough and worn to me. The cracks, the spots, the sagging… like they’re the first thing people see. If I’m talking to a banker or someone from the county, I feel like they’re noticing it and judging me for it.

My wife says I just look like a man who’s worked outdoors, but… I can’t quite see it that way.
When you worry about how rough your face and hands look, is it more about things that you know most people wouldn’t even notice, or do you feel like the changes are obvious to everyone?

It feels obvious to me.

I mean… maybe my wife’s right that other people don’t see it the way I do. But when I’m sitting with a banker or somebody from the county, I feel like they’re looking right at the cracks and spots, the sagging. Like it’s hard to miss.
